questions.topic: eGurukul · Pharmacotherapy of BPH, ED & Androgen Receptor Antagonists
questions.stem: A 60-year-old man came to the OPD with a persistent backache. Rectal examination revealed a single, hard, irregular nodule within his prostate. His prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level came to 100 ng/ml (normal 3.0 ng/ml) and a CT scan showed several enlarged pelvic lymph nodes and multiple sclerotic lesions in his spine. Which of the following pairs of drugs would be the most appropriate for the patient at this time?
questions.solutionHtml:
Leuprolide and flutamide
  • The patient’s signs and symptoms suggest prostate cancer and the exam results confirm the diagnosis of metastasized prostatic carcinoma.
  • Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) is the most used lab test for the early detection of prostate cancer, and spine metastases with prevalent necrotic lesions are the most common metastases of prostatic carcinoma.
  • The mainstay of treatment for metastasized prostate cancer is hormonal therapy. Because cancer is testosterone-dependent, hormonal manipulation focuses on reducing testosterone levels.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:326,932.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pharmacotherapy of BPH, ED & Androgen Receptor Antagonists
questions.stem: A 58-year-old man complained to his physician of fatigue, drowsiness, dizziness, and palpitations. He was recently diagnosed with bladder obstruction due to benign prostatic hyperplasia and had been taking a drug for 2 weeks. Which of the following drugs most likely caused the patient's symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tamsulosin
  • In a k/c/o Benign Hypertrophy of the Prostate (BHP) on treatment patient complaining of fatigability, drowsiness, dizziness, and palpitations is probably a side effect of Drug used in the treatment of Benign Hypertrophy of the Prostate (BHP).


  • Tamsulosin is a selective α 1 antagonist frequently used to counteract bladder obstruction due to prostatic hyperplasia. Fatigue, sleepiness, and dizziness are common adverse effects as seen in this patient most likely related to the drug-induced hypotension, palpitations are infrequently reported and are most likely related to the reflex tachycardia triggered by the drug-induced vasodilation.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: -156-157,932.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pharmacotherapy of BPH, ED & Androgen Receptor Antagonists
questions.stem: A 60-year-old man recently diagnosed with benign prostatic hyperplasia was scheduled for surgery. Which of the following drug classes would be contraindicated in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Antimuscarinics

In a k/c/o Benign prostatic hyperplasia patient antimuscarinics are absolutely contraindicated as they can precipitate acute urinary retention in BPH patients.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 124-127

questions.stem: Rahul, a 34-year-old man was referred to a psychiatrist because of irritability, worrying thoughts, palpitations, dry mouth, and insomnia of 1-month duration. The man had a history of alcohol abuse, but he was able to quit 1 year ago after psychological counseling and drug therapy. Recently, he suffered from erectile dysfunction, treated with sildenafil. A provisional diagnosis of generalized anxiety disorder was made, and cognitive behavioral therapy with drug treatment was prescribed. Which of the following drugs would be most appropriate for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Buspirone
  • A provisional diagnosis of generalized anxiety disorder was made.
  • Buspirone does not cause Sexual side effects and can be used in this patient with H/O erectile dysfunction.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 495-496

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pharmacotherapy of BPH, ED & Androgen Receptor Antagonists
questions.stem: A 58-year-old man suffering from benign prostatic hyperplasia was admitted to the hospital because of severe suprapubic pain and an inability to pass urine for the past 24 hours. On questioning, he said he had been taking diphenhydramine for a few days to relieve itching. Which of the following actions most likely mediated the adverse effect of the drug in this patient?

options.label: B
options.text: Constriction of the bladder's external sphincter

options.label: D
options.text: Relaxation of the bladder's internal sphincter

questions.solutionHtml:
Relaxation of the detrusor muscle

A Benign prostatic hyperplasia patient with acute urinary retention (severe suprapubic pain and an inability to pass urine for the past 24 hours.) with a history of taking diphenhydramine (first-generation antihistamine ) points towards its antimuscarinic action which relaxes the detrusor muscle and can precipitate acute urinary retention in BPH patients.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 183-186
